notes:
VERDICT: FAIL. Two majors - the attempt-2 fault was overcorrected past its target, and a locked feature was lost while doing it.

WHAT THE CORRECTION DID. Attempt 2's single major was a vertical drop 18-26 percent SHORT (0.612 waistband-depths against a drawn 0.744-0.831), with an instruction to lengthen it to about 0.78 WD. Attempt 3 lengthened it to 1.359 WD - past the target and out the other side by 46-79 percent. This is the same measurement, same normaliser, same sign convention, re-validated from scratch: render waistband depth 114.9 +/- 0.4 px over ten columns, drawing 103.4 +/- 0.5 px over nine columns, both stable enough to use. A second normalisation that needs no waistband at all - the drop-to-run-span aspect ratio, corrected for the measured 0.707 horizontal-to-vertical anisotropy - independently gives 1.77x where the waistband route gives 1.79x. Both endpoints were span-checked and neither is crop-limited.

LOCKED-FEATURE REGRESSION. 12 locked entries were carried in; 11 survived and one did not. The bar tack at the corner, which attempt 2 measured at peak luminance 94 against cloth 45.4 in a compact 19x30 px block, is absent: peak within 22 px of the new corner is 81 against cloth 49.7, the mean inside that radius is DARKER than the surrounding cloth, and the bright pixels are diffuse across a 67x69 px box rather than compact. A matched contrast-stretched side-by-side (evidence/c3_vs_c2_corner.png) makes it unambiguous. This is the fourth time on this project that a correction has fixed its target and broken something that already worked.

WHAT IMPROVED AND MUST NOT BE TOUCHED. Three of attempt 2's five minors are resolved or nearly so. The run's straightness went from 1.0 percent sagitta to 0.12 percent. The run's inclination residual against the waistband seam fell from 3.6 to 2.3 degrees. The context welt depth went from 0.16 WD (about half of drawn) to 0.373 WD (12 percent shallow). And the run's horizontal span, which attempt 2 measured as 17 percent short with an explicit "do NOT stretch" note, now reads 1.01x its perspective-predicted value - the note was heeded and the geometry landed. None of this may be traded away to fix the drop.

WHAT I CHECKED THAT TURNED OUT NOT TO BE AN ERROR. The corner now measures 91.0 degrees, which is closer to the option label's "90 degrees" than to the drawing's 96.3 - but the drawing wins, so this counts against the image, not for it. I nearly wrote the arm's 10.07 degree lean up as a major: it is 9.6 degrees off after normalising to the render's own front crease. But the render's outboard silhouette itself flares about 6 degrees through the pocket zone, and a pocket arm following the hip flare rather than plumb is physically defensible, so the honest residual is bounded between 3.8 and 9.6 degrees and I graded it minor. I also confirmed the enclosed quadrilateral formed by arm/waistband/crease/run is NOT a return of candidate-1's closed panel: the waistband seam and the crease are through-going features present in the drawing too, and the direct closure test below and right of the mouth finds nothing stronger than -8.9 against -29.1 on the mouth core.

MEASUREMENTS I COULD NOT MAKE. (1) No centimetre figures are recoverable - the tech pack carries no printed dimension callout, so every number here is a ratio against a landmark shared by both images; the spec's "90 degrees" is a label, not a drawing callout. (2) Belt loops are NOT a usable vertical landmark in this render - the six loop-edge traces gave fit residuals of 7.6 to 27.8 px because the loops are three-dimensional, curved and partly shadowed. I discarded them and used the front crease (residual 3.03 px over y=250..900) as the vertical reference, bounded by the outboard silhouette (residual 17.3 px, usable only as a bound). (3) I could not separate a genuine vertical stretch of the lower hip from a waistband-depth artefact: the waistband-seam to welt-upper-jet distance normalised by waistband depth reads 1.56-1.70 in the render against 1.39-1.49 in the drawing across seven belt-loop-matched positions, a consistent 13 percent excess. Rather than pick a side I applied that 13 percent as a generous allowance in favour of the image, and the drop still fails by 46 percent. (4) I still cannot call topstitching along the mouth either way - the twill's own diagonal dominates the periodicity - and the drawing shows a plain line with no stitch marks, so nothing is demanded. (5) There is a small dark spur below-left of the corner at about x=151-156, y=366-374 (luminance dipping to 14-38 against cloth 50-60, only a few pixels across). I could not classify it as a stitch tail, a bar-tack remnant or a render artefact, so I have recorded it here rather than raised it as a finding.

Nothing was written to data-store/ or public/images/generated/. New measurement crops saved to .craft-pipeline/suit-2pc/jeans-square/evidence/ (c3_pocket_zoom.png, c3_draw_pocket_zoom.png, c3_hp_pocket.png, c3_corner_zoom.png, c3_terminus_zoom.png, c3_armtop_zoom.png, c3_overlay.png, c3_draw_overlay.png, c3_vs_c2_corner.png). Pre-existing files in that folder were not modified.
